projects.title: Personal Website
projects.description: An interactive chatbot portfolio built using Next.js, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Three.js, Vercel AI SDK, and Gemini 2.0 Flash to showcase my builder/tinkerer identity through custom 3D voxel models and an AI twin.
highlights: Integrated an interactive LLM chatbot twin utilizing Gemini API & Vercel AI SDK to answer visitor inquiries.
Hand-crafted spatial 3D voxel models across all sections reflecting a block-builder design aesthetic inspired by Minecraft.
Implemented responsive OS-style window UI with full drag, resize, maximize, and theme switching controls.
reflection: In this fourth iteration of my personal website, I underwent multiple refactors to keep pace with evolving web standards, leveraging Next.js, Tailwind, and Three.js.
Hand-crafted 3D voxel models reflect my lifelong fascination with blocks and Minecraft.
Fine-tuning system prompts for the LLM chatbot presented challenges in ensuring context accuracy without hallucinations.

changes: 3rd major revamp with Next.js & Tailwind CSS.
Integrated LLM chatbot & interactive 3D voxel models.
Refined bio sections into structured high-context blocks.

projects.title: CellCollab
projects.short_description: Conway's Game of Life (CGL), but with multiplayer!
projects.description: A real-time, room-based multiplayer deployment of Conway's Game of Life allowing users to modify cellular matrices collaboratively on a uniform digital board using WebSockets and Socket.IO.
highlights: Engineered real-time room-based board synchronization via Socket.IO.
Features customizable settings including alternative color palettes, custom brush edits, and rule sets.
reflection: Built to explore WebSockets synchronization and state persistence in multiplayer board setups.
Tested board state broadcasts across high-latency simulated network conditions.

changes: Implemented more settings and improved layout.

projects.title: Astertris
projects.short_description: Tetris, but you're on a floating asteroid in space!
projects.description: A structural variation of Tetris utilizing localized radial gravity rules where Tetrominoes fall toward the center of a floating central asteroid, rendered in Java Swing using Object-Oriented Design and Data Structures.
highlights: Developed radial gravity block placement mechanics clearable symmetrically on any side of the asteroid.
Utilized Queue data structures for previewing upcoming pieces and 2D vectors to calculate state changes.
reflection: Created to practice Java Object-Oriented Design and Data Structure fundamentals ahead of NTU modules SC2002 & SC1007.
Overcame conventional downward gravity boundaries by modeling custom 2D vector attraction logic.

changes: UI improvements and scoring system integration.

projects.title: pySquidGame
projects.description: A playable Pygame application reproducing all 6 game stages from Netflix's 'Squid Game' (Red Light Green Light, Honeycomb, Tug of War, Marbles, Glass Stepping Stones, and Squid Game) plus Ddakji.
highlights: Implemented custom physics collisions and state management across 6 distinct minigames.
Updated button UI and game mechanics iteratively.
reflection: Initially prototyped 'Red Light Green Light' in 2021 before returning in 2025 to complete all remaining minigames.
Gained extensive experience managing game loops, collision detection, and multi-scene transitions in Pygame.

changes: Implemented Ddakji minigame and updated UI.
Bug fixes and RLGL physics improvements.

highlights: Built continuous ball motion physics and 10 custom golf course layouts.

frequently_asked_questions.question: Why did you build an AI assistant for your website?
frequently_asked_questions.answer: To provide recruiters and visitors with an instant, interactive way to query my background, skills, and metrics without scrolling through a traditional static resume. Additionally, people can also use my chatbot to get to know more about me, like my hobbies, interests, and tastes - preventing awkwardness when people reach out to ask about these basics!

frequently_asked_questions.question: Are you open to relocation?
frequently_asked_questions.answer: Not right now, because I'm focused on opportunities in Singapore while completing my computer science degree at Nanyang Technological University.

frequently_asked_questions.question: What are your biggest strengths and weaknesses?
frequently_asked_questions.answer: My greatest strength is my intense focus and reliability in delivering projects on time under tight constraints. My key area of continuous improvement is maintaining meticulous precision across high-velocity development cycles.

frequently_asked_questions.question: Who and what was your biggest influence in getting into computing?
frequently_asked_questions.answer: Minecraft was my all-time biggest inspiration for what I'm doing right now, because it allowed me to build and tinker with stuff just like how I use programming and web development to do the same things! Also, early exposure to technical creators like SethBling building complex Redstone logic gates in Minecraft inspired me to understand the principles behind computing systems.

frequently_asked_questions.question: Where do you see yourself in 5-10 years?
frequently_asked_questions.answer: In 5 years, I aim to be a proficient software engineer delivering scalable software products and personal tools. In 10 years, I see myself leveraging industry experience to architect impactful software solutions.

frequently_asked_questions.question: What are some things that keep you motivated in your career?
frequently_asked_questions.answer: One of the best things that keeps me motivated is that I generally like to build and tinker with things to help others carry out their daily needs and requirements seamlessly. I gain fulfillment if all of their objectives are successful, where a notable contribution involved me letting 300+ participants scan their attendance during my unit's non-training events. Because of this, I have the drive to keep on using my expertise to not only code, debug, and build applications, but also solve issues and simplify complex methodologies into easily accessible components.

frequently_asked_questions.question: What are your plans for 2027?
frequently_asked_questions.answer: Finish the semester strong with solid grades, as well as searching and preparing for internships!

frequently_asked_questions.question: What skillsets are you focusing on refining?
frequently_asked_questions.answer: Definitely Next.js, because most modern websites rely on Next.js nowadays. Additionally, one of my favorite things about Next.js is the fact that I can combine backend routes with frontend!

frequently_asked_questions.question: What are your favourite comfort foods?
frequently_asked_questions.answer: Sushi, Sashimi, Egg Fried Rice, and Tomahawk Steak (to max protein).

frequently_asked_questions.question: What are your biggest motivations to pursue fitness (especially running)?
frequently_asked_questions.answer: The main reason is for better mental health — for instance, running is a cheat code for me to get extra dopamine to stabilize my mood! Additionally, going to the gym to gain muscle helps me become more confident about having a healthy body. Physical health means little if mental health isn't prioritized as well.

frequently_asked_questions.question: Are you planning to combine code with fitness?
frequently_asked_questions.answer: Of course! I'm thinking about making new projects that involve applying my skillsets to help people live physically healthier lives!

frequently_asked_questions.question: Are you an introvert or an extrovert?
frequently_asked_questions.answer: Growing up, I was generally considered an introverted person — described as soft-spoken and preferring to recharge by myself. After NS and staying in hall, I opened up more and have gotten a lot more sociable, but I still definitely need my alone time! Right now, I can 'mask' as an extrovert — a lecturer once asked if I was naturally outspoken because I asked many questions and voiced out in class — but I still prefer to recharge by myself!

frequently_asked_questions.question: What are your pet peeves?
frequently_asked_questions.answer: No offense, but it's when I find UI components that look a bit off or vibe-coded, or parts of code that look too redundant (might be common among developers too).

frequently_asked_questions.question: I noticed you did not have any working/internship experience during your term break from May 2026 to Aug 2026. Why?
frequently_asked_questions.answer: One of the main reasons was that since I couldn't secure my desired internships at the time, I decided to use this break to not only work on this website, but also take time to reflect and recharge. The previous semester was academically intense, so I used this period to reset and prevent burnout, traveling to Japan with my mother and sister to explore Hokkaido and Tokyo!
